subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should this be fixed with a deliberate generic AgentCore control-flow-error contract, or should mid-turn precheck recovery stay entirely inside the embedded runner boundary?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable fix crosses the reusable agent-core package and embedded-runner recovery path; maintainers need to choose the long-term owner boundary before closing the issue.

options.title: Generic AgentCore control-flow contract
options.body: Define or document a generic non-failure control-flow marker that `Agent.handleRunFailure` honors, then land the focused fix with regression and real large-output proof.

options.title: Embedded-runner-only recovery
options.body: Keep AgentCore unaware of this OpenClaw-specific signal by changing the embedded runner flow so the signal never reaches generic failure streaming.

options.title: Fold the broader compaction PR
options.body: Use the older end-to-end PR only if maintainers also want its CLI already-compacted behavior and can require proof for that wider surface.

recommendation.title: Generic AgentCore control-flow contract
recommendation.body: Define or document a generic non-failure control-flow marker that `Agent.handleRunFailure` honors, then land the focused fix with regression and real large-output proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the recent commits that added the current central files and are the strongest current-main history signal for the agent/session boundary choice.
